newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees good demand for 30-year global.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees good demand for 30-year global.

text.p: Demand for Brazil's 30-year global and Brady buyback offer has been strong, with cash offers for the bond piling in, a Central Bank official said.

Fernando Antonio Gomes, head of the foreign capital department, said he expected the final pricing of the global to come in a bit above the spread given a 20-year 500 billion lire Eurobond placed Tuesday.

"Demand has been very good," Gomes told reporters in Brasilia, adding that the Central Bank Director of International Affairs, Gustavo Franco, was expected to announce the final results Wednesday in New York.
Gomes said the Central Bank was very pleased with a 348 basis points over equivalent U.S. Treasuries paid for Brazil's 20-year Eurolire issue. The bond was sold at par with an 11 percent coupon.
"The global ought to come in at a touch above that spread because it has a 30 year maturity," Gomes said.
Market talk in New York suggseted the global, given a minimum size of $1.0 billion, could grow to $2.0-3.0 billion and be issued at 370-380 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
Brazil's offer to buy back some Brady debt or swap it for the global expires Tuesday. Investors can also make cash offers for the 30-year bond up to 25 percent of its total value.
